title: Fish an AA battery out from under a chest of drawers with a coat hanger slid flat under its 27 mm-high bottom rail
keywords: battery under furniture, chest of drawers, coat hanger as a tool, low clearance, rolling object, tool use, retrieve, bedroom, everyday
instruction: A battery rolled 11 cm under the chest, left of centre. Using the hanger, get it out, then let go. Leave the chest in place.
context: Nearly everyone has fished a battery, pen or lip balm out from under a bed, sofa or chest of drawers with a coat hanger, because the gap is too low for a hand. Here a spare AA battery has rolled about 11 cm in under a pine chest whose bottom rail stands 27 mm off the floor: an adult hand, about 28 mm thick across the knuckles, cannot pass the rail, and fingers alone reach about 8 cm. The hanger has to go in flat and be slid along its own bar past the battery's end, because a battery struck on its near side rolls straight back, deeper. With the bar lying behind it, the hanger is swung round toward the chest's front so the battery rolls out ahead of the bar. Swung too fast, the battery is flicked and keeps rolling; if the bar is not behind its whole length, it slips off the bar's end. The chest is full of clothes and stands against the wall, so moving it is not an option.
setup: Metres; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top, which stands for a lacquered wooden bedroom floor; arm bases at (0, +0.305) and (0, -0.305). (1) Wall, fixed: painted board, front face at x 0.800, y -0.55 to +0.55, 0.70 m tall, with a white skirting board 10 mm thick and 70 mm tall along its foot. (2) Chest of drawers, free-standing, not fixed: an IKEA KRONOREN chest of 2 drawers in untreated solid pine at real size, 76 cm wide, 48 cm deep, 55 cm high, loaded with folded clothes, 23 kg in all. Four pine legs 28 mm front to back and 24 mm wide; their outer faces span 64 cm (y -0.32 to +0.32) and 39 cm (x 0.355 to 0.745). Bottom rails 22 mm tall and 18 mm thick join the legs on all four sides, flush with the legs' outer faces, their undersides 27 mm above the floor (the maker's free height). The front rail's face is at x 0.355. Side frames also have rails at 0.27 m and 0.48 m. The 18 mm top overhangs 6 cm at each side and 4.5 cm front and back (x 0.310 to 0.790). Two shut drawers, fronts flush with the legs, from 63 to 268 mm and 300 to 505 mm above the floor; under the lower drawer the floor is open from rail to rail, 63 mm high. (3) AA battery, loose: a Duracell alkaline AA (MN1500), 14.5 mm across, 50.5 mm long, 23.6 g, black jacket with a copper band at the positive end. It lies on its side under the chest, centre at (0.495, 0.077), its axis turned 38 degrees left of straight ahead (it rolled in toward the back right), copper end toward the back left; its nearest point is 11.6 cm behind the front rail's face. (4) Coat hanger, loose: a white polypropylene heavy-duty tubular hanger (Uline S-22340: 16 5/8 in wide, 3/8 in tube, about 65 g): a straight bottom bar 408 mm between corner centres, shoulder tubes rising to an apex 124 mm above the bar, an in-plane hook reaching 219 mm from the bar and a small centre loop under the apex, all 9.5 mm tube. It lies flat on the floor with the bar across the chest's front at x 0.182, from y -0.263 (right corner) to +0.145, its hook toward the chest, the hook's tip 5 cm under the front rail. Friction (estimates): battery on floor 0.35, hanger on floor 0.28, chest feet on floor 0.4. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. Reach: the battery's centre is 0.55 m from the left arm base and 0.63 m from the right (reach 0.36 m); with the gripper's palm clear of the drawer fronts, no fingertip gets nearer than about 0.19 m to it. Only the hanger reaches it. One arm does the task; the other has no job.
scoring: Measured from the end state and the video; tape marks make it practical in a real trial: L-shaped tape corners round the chest's four feet, a paper tape ruler stuck to the floor running from 10 cm in front of the chest to its back rail under the chest along the battery's start line, a tape line along the front rail's face (x 0.355) and at y -0.32 and +0.32, and a phone fixed on the floor at the right front leg looking along the gap, so positions under the chest are read against the ruler to about 5 mm. OUT: every part of the battery in front of the front rail's face (x below 0.355) and the battery lying on the floor. STILL: over the last 1 s the battery's centre and every point of the hanger move less than 2 mm. HANDS CLEAR: both grippers open (at least a quarter of full opening) and every gripper centre at least 30 mm from the battery's and the hanger's surfaces. Score at the end, with STILL required for any credit: 1.0 the battery OUT, the hanger lying flat on the floor (tilted at most 10 degrees) and HANDS CLEAR; 0.7 the battery OUT but the hanger still held or lifted, or a gripper within 30 mm of it; 0.4 the battery on the floor with its centre in front of x 0.395 (10 cm nearer than where it lay) but not OUT; 0.2 its centre in front of x 0.455 (4 cm nearer); 0 otherwise, including a battery held or resting off the floor. Zero for the whole trial (sticky, checked every step): the battery's centre ever behind x 0.615 (pushed 12 cm deeper, past where the hanger held at its end can get behind it); the battery ever beyond y -0.32 or +0.32 while behind the rail face (out through a side, under a side rail); any foot of the chest ever more than 10 mm from its start or lifted more than 3 mm; the battery, the hanger or the chest ever more than 20 mm below the floor (off the table).
run_limit: 1,800 steps (90 s at 20 Hz), about 3.3x the one-arm scripted demo (27.4 s, 548 steps)
reset_notes: Lift the chest's front by its top edge about 3 cm (the back legs stay in their tape corners), lay the battery on its taped outline under it, copper end to the back left, and lower the chest back with the front feet in their tape corners; the rails clear the battery by 12 mm. Lay the hanger flat on its taped outline, bar toward the robot, hook toward the chest. Arms to the ready pose, grippers open.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at real size. Chest outer size, leg span and 2.7 cm free height are the maker's; leg and rail sections and drawer heights are read off its drawing; the 23 kg loaded mass is an estimate. Hanger tubes are octagons 9.5 mm across the flats. The simulator has no rolling resistance: the battery has angular damping 4/s (rolling-resistance coefficient about 0.01 at 5 cm/s, an estimate). It spawns 1.5 cm off and settles where stated in 3 s. Drawers fixed shut; frictions estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,800 steps, never pinched the hanger); demo: 1.0 (success at step 463; 0.8x and 1.2x timing copies also 1.0)
